questions.q: What is the model owner accountable for, according to the lesson?
options: Approving their own model for deployment with no outside review
Writing the model's training code line by line
The business outcome of a specific model's decisions in production
Only the physical servers the model runs on
questions.explain: The lesson defines the model owner as the business-side role accountable for a model's outcomes, not the technical build itself.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say independent validation matters, separate from the build team?
options: Because model builders are generally untrustworthy people
Because only validators are legally allowed to use computers
Because the people who built the model share the same blind spots that shaped it and can't fully audit their own work
Because independent validators are required to write all the model's code
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that independence isn't about distrust — it's that builders share the same blind spots as what they built.

questions.q: What role does the AI governance council play, per the lesson?
options: Only handles customer support tickets
Personally retrains every deployed model each week
Approves new AI use cases, sets policy, and reviews incidents
Replaces the need for a model owner entirely
questions.explain: The council plays a cross-functional oversight role — the same role an existing data governance council already plays, now with AI items on its agenda.

questions.q: Per the lesson's rule of thumb, who owns whether an AI use case should have been approved at all?
options: The model builder alone
The end customer
No one — this is left intentionally undecided
The governance council
questions.explain: The lesson assigns this specific accountability to the council, distinct from the owner's business accountability and the builder's technical accountability.

questions.q: How does the lesson describe the relationship between AI governance roles and data governance roles?
options: AI governance roles are close relatives of data governance roles, applied one layer up to models
AI governance eliminates the need for data governance roles
Data governance roles only apply to spreadsheets, never to models
They are entirely unrelated and share no structure
questions.explain: The lesson frames AI governance roles as extensions of familiar data governance roles like owner, steward, and council.
